title: CHK2 regulates MUS81-dependent DSBs in response to replication stress and BRCA2 deficiency.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Read the paper's data availability statement; queried PRIDE for PXD064334 (10 files: two raw Bruker .d.zip of 85 MB and 77 MB, two MGF peak lists, two Mascot .dat, two mzIdentML results, two PDF Mascot views) and MassIVE MSV000101714 metadata; downloaded and parsed both mzIdentML result files. 7278.mzid holds 11 peptide-spectrum matches over 4 protein entries (MUS81_HUMAN, CHK2_HUMAN plus 2 spurious hits); 7279.mzid holds 41 peptide-spectrum matches over 18 protein entries, mostly short spurious peptides. Total deposited identifications: 52 rows about one protein.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: All quantitative biology in the paper (counts of DNA double-strand-break foci per cell, DNA fibre-assay track lengths, western-blot intensities, cell-survival curves) is described in the figures only; the paper states these datasets are 'available at request'. The MassIVE record's design (3 conditions x 4 replicates = 12 targeted runs of two MUS81 peptides) comes from the repository summary, not from files I opened.

a1_downloadable.note: The data availability statement says the generated datasets 'are available at request through submission on public repositories' - an explicit available-on-request failure. Only the mass-spectrometry side is actually deposited (PRIDE PXD064334, MassIVE MSV000101714); the microscopy, fibre-assay and survival measurements that make up the paper's results are not in any repository.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No label column exists anywhere. The deposited files are peptide identification results (mzIdentML) and raw spectra; a prediction target (e.g. 'is this residue phosphorylated by CHK2') would have to be constructed by hand from 52 peptide-spectrum matches plus figure panels.

a3_inputs_present.note: Protein sequences for the two relevant proteins (MUS81 and CHK2, human) are trivially retrievable from UniProt, and peptide sequences are present in the mzIdentML files. This is the only Part A item that passes cleanly.

a4_units_stated.note: The deposited results carry Mascot scores and mass tolerances but no measured quantity with units that could serve as a target; the paper's quantitative panels (foci per cell, fibre length in kb) have units in the figure axes but the underlying numbers are not released.

a5_enough_rows.note: Verified by parsing both mzIdentML files: 11 + 41 = 52 peptide-spectrum matches in total, covering essentially one protein (MUS81) and its kinase (CHK2). The checklist floor is ~1,500 labelled rows, or ~400 for classification.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~0.14 MB of result files; ~163 MB if the two raw Bruker .d.zip archives were also taken
a6_fits_laptop.note: Size is not the problem here - everything fits trivially on a laptop. There is simply almost nothing in it.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be assessed: the paper reports no row or sample counts for a tabular dataset, and the MassIVE record states 12 targeted runs whose processed output I could not locate as a table, so there is nothing to reconcile.

a8_label_provenance.note: The nearest thing to a label is a phosphosite assignment produced by the Mascot search engine with a delta-score rule, i.e. a software call on spectra, not an independent measurement - and there are 52 such calls. No usable, independently measured label exists.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (a protein language model) would be the natural backbone for any kinase-substrate phosphosite task
backbone.hardware: CPU-only laptop would suffice for the small ESM-2 checkpoints, if there were data to fit a head on
backbone.licence: ESM-2 is MIT-licensed; the deposited proteomics is CC0, so licensing would not have blocked anything

integration.partner_dataset: PhosphoSitePlus or EPSD (databases of experimentally reported protein phosphorylation sites), joinable to UniProt accessions
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: A general question exists - which serine/threonine residues a given checkpoint kinase phosphorylates - but this paper contributes 52 peptide-spectrum matches on a single protein, so it adds nothing measurable to that question.

controls.positive_control: Not applicable - no model was proposed because there is no dataset to model.
controls.external_validation: PhosphoSitePlus already records MUS81 phosphosites, so the paper's own finding could be checked against it, but that is a lookup, not a validation of any model.

honest_claim_h3: No honest modelling claim can be made from this paper's released data: the only public files are 52 peptide-spectrum matches on MUS81 and CHK2, and every quantitative cell-biology measurement is available only on request.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use protein sequence around each serine or threonine to predict whether the checkpoint kinase CHK2 phosphorylates that site.
plain_idea.train_on: The project considered would show the model a short stretch of protein sequence centred on a candidate serine or threonine. This paper supplies only 52 peptide-spectrum matches on one protein, far too few to train anything.
plain_idea.predict: Whether that residue is phosphorylated by CHK2. In this paper the answer comes from a Mascot database search of mass spectra from an in vitro kinase reaction, which is a software assignment on 52 spectra rather than a large measured table.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Knowing which residues a checkpoint kinase modifies would help cancer-biology labs working on BRCA2-mutant tumours pick mutants to test, but this paper cannot support that project; the labelled data would have to come almost entirely from public phosphosite databases instead.

ml_idea: None viable from this paper. The only conceivable task - predicting CHK2 phosphorylation sites from sequence - would have to be built almost entirely from external resources (PhosphoSitePlus, EPSD), with this paper contributing at most a handful of held-out positives on MUS81.

effort.compute_note: Sizes are measured from the PRIDE file listing and the two mzIdentML files I downloaded and parsed; no modelling estimates are given because there is no dataset to model.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Open the deposited mzIdentML files and count peptide-spectrum matches - it took one command and returned 52, which ends the project immediately.

verdict_reason: A mechanistic cell-biology paper, not a data resource. The data availability statement says the generated datasets are 'available at request' (A1 fail), and the only deposited files - PRIDE PXD064334 and MassIVE MSV000101714 - contain 52 peptide-spectrum matches on MUS81 and CHK2 plus two raw Bruker runs, verified by parsing both result files. No label column, no units, no rows (A2, A4, A5, A8 all fail).
